title: Composition with Yellow, Red, Black, Blue, and Gray
lede: One of the first paintings in Mondrian’s mature neoplastic manner: a white square at the center, ringed by black, gray, and primary planes, divided by black lines of one weight.
summary: White center square, red strip at left, yellow at top and right, a dark blue plane below, black lines. Piet Mondrian, 1920.

source.label: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam: Compositie met geel, rood, zwart, blauw en grijs

evidence.note: Inspected the Wikimedia Commons image (from RKD image 218858; 1000 × 860 px, viewed at 960 px) of the painting in the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam, object A 9864. The Stedelijk collection page renders with JavaScript and returned no text to the fetch tool.

styles.note: A canonical neoplastic painting of 1920: only horizontal and vertical lines, flat primaries with black, white, and several grays, and an asymmetric balance around a white center.

context: The Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam holds the painting as object A 9864, dated 1920. [Wikidata Q24058759](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q24058759) gives the same number and date.

Commons lists it with Mondrian’s works of his second Paris period, 1920–1937. [Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Piet_Mondriaan_-_Composition_with_yellow,_red,_black,_blue_and_gray_-_A_9864_-_Stedelijk_Museum_Amsterdam.jpg).
observed: A large white square fills the center; a flat yellow plane sits above it and a dark, grayish blue plane below it.
A tall red strip runs down the left edge; two large black planes flank the white square at left and top right.
A second yellow plane stands at the right, above small light-gray cells; gray planes fill the corners.
Black lines of about the same width divide every plane; several run to the edge of the canvas, and some stop short of it at the top and bottom.
The initials and date “PM 20” are painted at lower left.
Paint texture and fine cracks are visible in the white and gray planes.
interpretation: The blue is dark and gray, the red is a warm earth red, and black and gray planes cover as much area as the primaries. The pure, bright primaries of later “Mondrian” pastiche are not yet here.
The composition is centered on the white square but not symmetric: the color planes are distributed to the edges, which fits the rubric’s asymmetric balance.
borrow: Put a large neutral plane at the center and push the colors to the edges.
Use black planes as well as black lines, so black carries weight, not only structure.

images.alt: Abstract painting: a large white square in the center, yellow planes above it and at the right, a dark grayish blue plane below it, a red strip along the left edge, two black planes, and light gray cells, all divided by black horizontal and vertical lines.
images.caption: Piet Mondrian, Composition with Yellow, Red, Black, Blue, and Gray, 1920. Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam, A 9864. Image from [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Piet_Mondriaan_-_Composition_with_yellow,_red,_black,_blue_and_gray_-_A_9864_-_Stedelijk_Museum_Amsterdam.jpg), public domain.

rights.statement: Commons marks the image PD-Art with PD-old-auto-expired: Mondrian died in 1944, so his work is public domain in the Netherlands and the EU since 2015. The painting dates from 1920; it is public domain in the United States as a work published before 1931, and also under the life-plus-70 rule if it counts as unpublished.
